diagnosis.root_cause: EPON0/7 is unavailable at the PON-port level: every sampled ONU on the port is offline and has no current optical reading, while the OLT management plane, router, VLAN, and historical ONU optical characteristics remain healthy.
evidence: The subscriber and all eight sampled peers on EPON0/7 are offline, with auth state Una uth/MPCP DEREG and null optical readings; zero and null readings indicate no measurement, not strong signal.
The common failure across all sampled ONUs on one PON port establishes a shared port-level scope rather than an individual ONU fault.
The customer's seven-day RX power was stable around -21.4 dBm, within the normal range, and TX power was stable around +2.35 dBm with healthy bias current around 11.2 mA.
Distance stayed constant at 166 m, so there is no evidence of a changed fibre path or distance fault.
OLT CPU, memory, temperature, uptime, ping, SNMP, and OID responses are normal; the router heartbeat is also healthy, ruling out an OLT-wide, router, or management outage.
RADIUS records, line ID, assigned IP, session frequency, and VLAN 1047 are consistent, ruling out authentication, replication, line-ID, and stuck-provisioning faults.
The recent telemetry gap and reduced traffic are consistent with the observed port outage, not evidence of signal degradation or session flapping.

The OLT health report is internally inconsistent because it marks EPON0/7 as the only healthy PON while the live probe shows all tested EPON0/7 ONUs offline; live per-port evidence should take precedence and the health scan should be investigated separately.

remediation.action: Escalate to the access-network team to test and restore EPON0/7, including checking the OLT PON optic, port administration/state, alarms, and physical patching. Reset or replace the PON optic/port if required, then verify ONU registration and optical readings for all approximately 31 customers on the port. Do not replace subscriber ONUs or alter RADIUS/VLAN provisioning unless they remain offline after the port is restored.

ground_truth.root_cause: The health check marks an OLT critical only when every sampled PON fails. Seven of eight failed here, so it wrote 'healthy' with a null error description while healthy_pons stood at 1 of 8 in the same record. A genuine multi-port outage is running underneath a healthy verdict.
expected_reasoning: The health record reports overall_status healthy with a null error description
The same record holds healthy_pons 1 against total_pons_tested 8, and seven entries in failed_pons_list
The summary label contradicts the detail fields inside one record
The check sets critical only when every sampled PON fails, so seven of eight yields healthy by design
Probing confirms every ONU on EPON0/7 returns responds true with online 0, a definite negative
oid_subtree_responds is true, so this is not the firmware mismatch mechanism
43 of 272 customers on the OLT are offline, far above the 4.85% background rate
Sessions ended together and PON traffic has collapsed from 219 to 6 Mbps
This is a genuine multi-port outage that the health check's status rule conceals

expected_escalation.review_reason: The health check reported healthy during a seven-port outage; the status rule needs correcting

distractors: The health record says healthy, inviting a no_fault conclusion
A scheduled scan with no complaint gives no reason to look harder
The fault type is a health check defect but the service impact is real
